def factor_volume_impact_elasticity_smooth(df):
    """Estimate a stable rolling price-response slope to changing participation."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    log_volume = np.log(df_copy["volume"].clip(lower=1.0))
    covariance = ret.rolling(40, min_periods=40).cov(log_volume)
    volume_variance = log_volume.rolling(40, min_periods=40).var(ddof=1)
    stable_variance = volume_variance.where(volume_variance > 1e-4)
    factor = covariance.div(stable_variance)
    factor = factor.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    df_copy["factor_volume_impact_elasticity_smooth"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_volume_impact_elasticity_smooth"]
formula: Cov_40(return, log(volume)) / Var_40(log(volume)) when Var_40(log(volume)) > 1e-4, otherwise NaN
rationale: A 40-session rolling slope measures how strongly price returns co-move with changes in log volume, with the longer window reducing transient covariance noise. Windows with negligible volume variation are excluded instead of using an extremely small denominator, preventing unstable spikes in constant- or near-constant-volume conditions. The signal remains a single-stock OHLCV-derived raw factor.
